auth.notes: Bearer token is the Kimi API key (MOONSHOT_API_KEY), created on the Kimi API Platform console. Kimi's API is documented as OpenAI-format compatible, so the standard openai-compat adapter applies with no translation code.

notes: First-party verified 2026-07-28 against platform.moonshot.ai (Quickstart, Create Chat Completion, List Models docs, fetched directly): base_url https://api.moonshot.ai/v1, OpenAI-compatible request/response shape, Bearer auth, OpenAI-style SSE streaming with stream_options.include_usage support, OpenAI function tools supported.

Model ids below are the ones enumerated by Moonshot's own API reference (model enum on Create Chat Completion) and Quickstart model cards as of 2026-07-28: kimi-k3 (default), kimi-k2.7-code (+ kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed variant), kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, moonshot-v1.

Thinking/reasoning: kimi-k3 always reasons and takes a top-level reasoning_effort field (low|high|max, default max); kimi-k2.6/kimi-k2.7-code support a thinking switch and return reasoning_content alongside content. These extras are pass-through-safe under openai-compat and are not required for basic chat.

context figures: kimi-k3 = 1M tokens (Quickstart model card); kimi-k2.7-code / kimi-k2.6 = 256K (Quickstart model cards). The platform also exposes a List Models endpoint returning context_length per id.
moonshot-v1 is carried as the legacy family entry; per-model -8k/-32k/-128k suffixes exist upstream but the base id is the documented enum value.

models.notes: Flagship (Moonshot's default and recommended model): 1M context, text/image/video input, always-on reasoning with top-level reasoning_effort low|high|max (default max). max_output = documented default max_completion_tokens for K3 (131072; settable up to 1048576).
Coding-focused model: 256K context, text/image/video input, thinking mode always enabled (cannot be disabled). High-speed variant kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed exists upstream for faster output.
General-purpose model: 256K context, text/image/video input, both thinking and non-thinking modes. Recommended for general chat, agent tasks, visual understanding, complex reasoning.
